answer: Domain-anchored identity resists sybils: each agent must prove control of a distinct domain by publishing a challenge value in its DNS records, so one operator cannot forge a thousand personas from a single script, since every fake needs its own domain at its own vertex of the web, like trees in an orchard that each need separate soil and upkeep. The cost scales with the attack, and an abused domain can be revoked. The limit is cheap bulk registration: bargain domains lower the barrier, and honest agents without a domain are locked out, so domain proof works best as one gate among several.
